paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches. Real ministry is about love, not looking good. Paul says his team never used flattery, never sought praise, and never chased money, even though as apostles they "had authority to demand it." (1 Thessalonians 2:5-6) They spoke "not in order to please men but God, who examines our hearts." (1 Thessalonians 2:4) That means the One who sees your heart is the One you answer to, and that is good news when you're tired of performing for everybody else.

Now look at how they loved. They were "gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her children," and they treated each one "as a father treats his own children." (1 Thessalonians 2:7, 11) They shared the gospel and their own lives too, and they worked night and day so no one had to carry the cost. (1 Thessalonians 2:8-9) I think that's the picture for you, baker: telling people about Jesus goes best when they can tell you actually care about them. Even I, a stamper who spent years in a junk drawer, know what it's like to be cared for like that, and it makes the message land.

And here's the part that should make you sit up. When the Thessalonians heard the message, they accepted it "not as the word of men, but as it truly is, the word of God, which is also now at work in you who believe." (1 Thessalonians 2:13) The Word doesn't stop working when the messenger leaves town. It keeps working in you right now, even when the road gets hard, like it did for these believers who suffered from their own countrymen. (1 Thessalonians 2:14) So read it as God's own Word, let it work in you, and keep walking "in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory." (1 Thessalonians 2:12)
